claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure comprising an fcc matrix and a hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
The fcc matrix in the dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy is ferromagnetic.
The isolated fcc phase typically has coercivity below approximately 100 Oe because its orbital moments are limited.
Rapid quenching stabilizes the dual fcc/C14 microstructure in FeCoNiTi.
The C14 phase remains stable at 400 K.
The relevant microstructure consists of a continuous fcc matrix containing dispersed C14 Laves-phase precipitates.
Coexistence with the C14 phase can increase coercivity while decreasing saturation magnetization relative to a single-phase ferromagnetic alloy.
The Ti-rich C14 sublattice couples antiferromagnetically to the Fe-Co-Ni fcc matrix.
Antiferromagnetic interfacial coupling suppresses the net saturation magnetization of the fcc phase.
The fcc/C14 phase boundary acts as a magnetic-domain-wall pinning site.
Ti atoms in the C14 phase possess local magnetic moments.
The Ti local moments align antiferromagnetically with adjacent Fe, Co, and Ni moments in the fcc phase.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling reduces the effective magnetic moment per atom in the fcc phase.
The fcc/C14 interface generates a large local magnetocrystalline-anisotropy energy.
The interfacial anisotropy creates deep energy wells that pin domain walls and thereby increase coercivity beyond the intrinsic fcc limit.
The dual-phase alloy will have lower saturation magnetization than a pure fcc FeCoNi alloy.
The dual-phase alloy will exhibit a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The proposed mechanism ceases to apply if the C14 phase is amorphous, its fraction is too low, or the temperature exceeds the relevant magnetic ordering temperatures.
A spin-polarized DFT calculation using an explicit fcc/C14 interface model can test the fcc spin density of states and magnetic alignment at the interface.
Temperature-dependent comparison of dual-phase, C14-dominant, and single-phase fcc samples can distinguish phase-specific magnetic behavior.

contradictions.description: The mediator and mechanism fields present an antiferromagnetically ordered Ti sublattice and Ti-to-Fe/Co/Ni coupling as established features, whereas the uncertainty field states that the Ti-sublattice ordering is not experimentally confirmed and the coupling strength is unknown.
The stated applicable microstructure contains dispersed C14 precipitates, but the boundary field implies that applicability requires enough C14 to form a continuous network.

The mechanism assigns coercivity enhancement primarily to fcc/C14 interfaces, so lower coercivity in a C14-dominant sample than in the dual-phase sample would be compatible with reduced interfacial pinning rather than evidence that C14 interfaces do not enhance pinning. Criterion (a) is therefore not a logically decisive falsifier of the stated mechanism.
